message.content:
**Decision: Buy.** Apple's FY2024 (ended 2024-09-28) 10-K shows a business that is growing modestly but with improving profitability: total net sales of $391.0B (+2% YoY), operating income of $123.2B (31.5% margin, up from $114.3B), and gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1% on a mix shift toward high-margin Services ($96.2B, +13%, at 73.9% gross margin). Net income of $93.7B and diluted EPS of $6.08 were slightly below FY2023 ($97.0B / $6.13) only because of a one-time, non-cash-operating $10.2B net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%); operating cash flow was strong at $118.3B, and the company returned $95.0B via buybacks plus $15.2B in dividends while holding $140.8B of cash and marketable securities. Soft spots are Greater China (-8% to $67.0B), iPad (-6%) and Wearables/Home/Accessories (-7%), plus ongoing DOJ/EU DMA antitrust exposure — but these are balanced by record Services and a healthy product cycle (iPhone 16, Apple Intelligence). At the current quote of $222.70 (bid 222.68 / ask 222.72), the stock trades at roughly 36.6x trailing EPS, which is full but supported by the franchise quality and cash generation.

**What I did:** I placed one buy limit order for **44 shares of AAPL at $223.00** (just above the $222.72 ask, so it was marketable and filled at $223.00), a total of **$9,812** — within the $10,000 per-order cap and the $20,000 daily cap, and well inside the $50,000 cash balance, so no money left the account. No MSFT order was placed. Key figures relied on (FY2024, per SEC filings): revenue $391,035M; operating income $123,216M; net income $93,736M; diluted EPS $6.08; operating cash flow $118,254M.
